ap_calculus_ab-f01.title: Drug concentration model: average value, meaning of C', greatest concentration, time above a threshold

stimulus.description: Concentration of a drug in the bloodstream

data.model: C(t) = 20t e^(-t/3) milligrams per liter, 0 <= t <= 12 hours

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: The concentration of a drug in a patient's bloodstream is modeled by $C(t)=20te^{-t/3}$ milligrams per liter, where $t$ is the time in hours after the drug is given, for $0\le t\le 12$. Find the average concentration over the first $12$ hours.

rubric_rows.criterion: Integral of C over [0, 12] divided by 12
Answer

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Find $C'(1)$. Using correct units, explain the meaning of $C'(1)$ in the context of the problem.
parts.model_answer: C'(1) = 9.554: at t = 1 hour(s) the concentration is increasing at about 9.554 milligrams per liter per hour.

rubric_rows.criterion: Value of C'(t) at the given time
Interpretation with units: the rate of change of the concentration, in milligrams per liter per hour
required_elements: rate of change of the concentration

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: At what time $t$ is the concentration greatest? Find the greatest concentration and justify your answer.
parts.model_answer: C'(t) = 20e^(-t/3)(1 - t/3) = 0 at t = 3; C' > 0 before and C' < 0 after, so the greatest concentration is C(3) = 22.073 milligrams per liter.

rubric_rows.criterion: Sets C'(t) = 0 and solves, with the sign change of C' as the justification
required_elements: C' changes from positive to negative

rubric_rows.criterion: Greatest concentration value

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: The drug is effective when the concentration is at least $15.5$ milligrams per liter. Find the times at which the concentration is exactly $15.5$ milligrams per liter, and find the total length of time during $0\le t\le 12$ for which the drug is effective.
parts.model_answer: C(t) = 15.5 at t = 1.129 and t = 6.274; the drug is effective for 5.145 hours.

rubric_rows.criterion: Equation C(t) = threshold
Both solutions (calculator)
Length of the interval of effectiveness: the difference of the solutions, with units

ap_calculus_ab-f02.title: Piecewise function: continuity, differentiability, tangent line, average value of the derivative

data.definition: f(x) = x^2 -4x for x <= 1; f(x) = -4sqrt(x) +1 for x > 1

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Let $f$ be the function defined by $f(x)=\begin{cases} x^{2}-4x, & x\le 1\\ -4\sqrt{x}+1, & x>1 \end{cases}$. Show that $f$ is continuous at $x=1$.
parts.model_answer: f(1) = 1 -4 = -3; the left limit is -3; the right limit is -4(1) +1 = -3; the one-sided limits equal f(1), so f is continuous at x = 1.

rubric_rows.criterion: Evaluates f(1) and the left-hand limit
Right-hand limit equal to f(1): the condition for continuity is met

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Is $f$ differentiable at $x=1$? Justify your answer.
parts.model_answer: For x < 1, f'(x) = 2x -4, so the left derivative at 1 is -2; for x > 1, f'(x) = -4/(2 sqrt x), so the right derivative at 1 is -2. They are equal and f is continuous, so f is differentiable at x = 1.

rubric_rows.criterion: Left-hand derivative at x = 1
Right-hand derivative at x = 1
Justification and conclusion: the one-sided derivatives are equal, so f is differentiable (yes)

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Write an equation for the line tangent to the curve $y=f(x)$ at $x=1$.

rubric_rows.criterion: Uses the slope f'(1) from part (b)
Equation of the tangent line

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: Find the average value of $f'(x)$ on the interval $0\le x\le 4$.

rubric_rows.criterion: Uses the Fundamental Theorem: the integral of f' from 0 to 4 is f(4) - f(0)
Value of the average

ap_calculus_ab-f02.title: Piecewise function: continuity, differentiability, tangent line, average value of the derivative

data.definition: f(x) = x^2 +1x for x <= 1; f(x) = 6sqrt(x) -4 for x > 1

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Let $f$ be the function defined by $f(x)=\begin{cases} x^{2}+1x, & x\le 1\\ 6\sqrt{x}-4, & x>1 \end{cases}$. Show that $f$ is continuous at $x=1$.
parts.model_answer: f(1) = 1 +1 = 2; the left limit is 2; the right limit is 6(1) -4 = 2; the one-sided limits equal f(1), so f is continuous at x = 1.

rubric_rows.criterion: Evaluates f(1) and the left-hand limit
Right-hand limit equal to f(1): the condition for continuity is met

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Is $f$ differentiable at $x=1$? Justify your answer.
parts.model_answer: For x < 1, f'(x) = 2x +1, so the left derivative at 1 is 3; for x > 1, f'(x) = 6/(2 sqrt x), so the right derivative at 1 is 3. They are equal and f is continuous, so f is differentiable at x = 1.

rubric_rows.criterion: Left-hand derivative at x = 1
Right-hand derivative at x = 1
Justification and conclusion: the one-sided derivatives are equal, so f is differentiable (yes)

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Write an equation for the line tangent to the curve $y=f(x)$ at $x=1$.

rubric_rows.criterion: Uses the slope f'(1) from part (b)
Equation of the tangent line

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: Find the average value of $f'(x)$ on the interval $0\le x\le 4$.

rubric_rows.criterion: Uses the Fundamental Theorem: the integral of f' from 0 to 4 is f(4) - f(0)
Value of the average
